title: The Program That Rewrites Its Own Address
pitch: One 32-byte memory holds both instructions and data. A stored-program loop learns to walk an array by editing its own next fetch.

story.name: sum3_loop
story.definition: This routine walks three array cells by rewriting the ADD operand.
story.body:
LD 28       ; Restore the accumulated total for the next item.
ADD 29      ; Add the item at the operand byte, address 3.
ST 28       ; Save the new total.
LD 3        ; Read the ADD operand from the code.
ADDI 1      ; Advance the address without an index register.
ST 3        ; Rewrite the ADD operand in place.
LD 27       ; Read the remaining-item counter.
ADDI 255    ; Subtract one modulo 256.
ST 27       ; Save the remaining-item counter.
JZ @done    ; Stop after exactly three iterations.
JMP 0       ; Process the next item.
done: LD 28 ; Return the saved total.
HALT        ; Stop execution.

contract.guarantees: sum of three 0..15 bytes modulo 256; fresh call scratch

story.ascii: op sum3_loop(s: VN) -> VN = let routine_base = 0 in let routine_bytes = "021c041d031c020308010303021b08ff031b07160600021c0000" in rec r0(s) = if is_halted(s) then s else r0(step(s)) measure fuel in r0(s) L1

examples.text: This routine walks three array cells by rewriting the ADD operand.

story.name: sum3_restored
story.definition: This routine restores the operand before a repeated three-cell sum.
story.body:
LDI 29      ; Select the first array cell.
ST 7        ; Restore the ADD operand before each call.
loop: LD 27 ; Load the running sum (caller supplies zero).
ADD 29      ; Add the current array cell, initially 29.
ST 27       ; Save the updated sum.
LD 7        ; Read the operand byte from the ADD instruction.
ADDI 1      ; Advance the data address.
ST 7        ; Patch the operand byte for the next iteration.
SUB 28      ; Compare with the exclusive end address, 32.
JZ @done    ; Exit when all three cells have been read.
JMP @loop   ; Otherwise repeat with the patched ADD.
done: LD 27 ; Return the total.
HALT        ; Stop execution.

contract.guarantees: two calls after caller resets accumulator and scratch 27

story.ascii: op sum3_restored(s: VN) -> VN = let routine_base = 0 in let routine_bytes = "011d0307021b041d031b020708010307051c07160604021b0000" in rec r0(s) = if is_halted(s) then s else r0(step(s)) measure fuel in r0(s) L2

examples.text: This routine restores the operand before a repeated three-cell sum.

story.name: source_add

story.ascii: op source_add(s: VN) -> VN = let routine_base = 0 in let routine_bytes = "021c041d0000" in rec r0(s) = if is_halted(s) then s else r0(step(s)) measure fuel in r0(s) L1

story.name: relocated_add
story.definition: This routine is reverified at address 12 after copying and rewriting both operands.
story.body:
LD 30 ; Retarget first absolute load.
ADD 31 ; Retarget second absolute load.
HALT ; Stop.

contract.guarantees: adds two relocated bytes modulo 256

story.ascii: op relocated_add(s: VN) -> VN = let routine_base = 12 in let routine_bytes = "021e041f0000" in rec r0(s) = if is_halted(s) then s else r0(step(s)) measure fuel in r0(s) L2

examples.text: This routine is reverified at address 12 after copying and rewriting both operands.

story.name: restore_idempotent
story.definition: This scoped law says resetting the same operand twice has the same full-state effect as resetting it once.

scope.domain: exactly the three listed operand images at address 7: 32, 29, 0

contract.guarantees: resetting the operand twice equals resetting it once

over.domain: exactly the three listed operand images at address 7: 32, 29, 0

examples.text: Both repaired code images are equal on this checked input.

story.ascii: law #restore_idempotent: eq(reset_operand(reset_operand(s)), reset_operand(s)) for s: VN L3

story.name: fix
story.definition: This bounded fixpoint reapplies operand repair until the complete code image stops changing.

scope.domain: two operand images 32 and 29; stable after at most two repairs

contract.guarantees: reapply repair until the code image stabilizes

over.domain: two operand images 32 and 29; stable after at most two repairs

examples.text: Repair until the image stabilizes within two iterations.

story.ascii: comb @fix[repair: A -> A](x: A, height: A) -> A = rec fix_local(state, remaining) = if comb_positive(remaining) then let next_state = repair(state) in if eq(state, next_state) then next_state else fix_local(next_state, comb_dec(remaining)) else fail("not_stable") measure remaining in fix_local(x, height) L1

story.name: relocate_12
story.definition: This partial bridge copies the routine to base 12 and retargets its absolute operands, preserving the executed accumulator on its stated scope.

scope.domain: all four source input pairs in 0..1; six-byte source at 0, free target at 12, matching data at 28..31

contract.guarantees: retargeted copy preserves the executed accumulator

over.domain: all four source input pairs in 0..1; six-byte source at 0, free target at 12, matching data at 28..31

examples.text: Copy and retarget a routine in the partial bridge domain.

story.ascii: bridge ~relocate_12: vn -> vn = relocate_add(x) where if eq(peek(x, 0), 2) then (if eq(peek(x, 1), 28) then (if eq(peek(x, 2), 4) then (if eq(peek(x, 3), 29) then (if eq(peek(x, 4), 0) then (if eq(peek(x, 5), 0) then (if eq(get_pc(x), 0) then (if eq(peek(x, 28), peek(x, 30)) then (if eq(peek(x, 29), peek(x, 31)) then true else false) else false) else false) else false) else false) else false) else false) else false) else false commutes (source_result -> target_result) L3

showcase.prompt: VN<32 cells, pc=0, a=0, mem[0..19]=[1, 5, 3, 16, 2, 28, 4, 29, 3, 27, 2, 27, 4, 30, 6, 16, 4, 31, 0, 0], mem[28..31]=[17,9,4,6]; all other cells are 0>: give final ?a{s} and executed instructions within fuel 30. Bytes at overlapping addresses are given by the listed program.
showcase.why_hard: ST 16 turns the later ADD 31 into SUB 31; the program also saves and reloads an intermediate result.
showcase.check: Run with fuel 30; compare the complete final state and the exact instruction count.

showcase.why_hard: The loop computes 30, patches the operand of ST at 25, then writes HALT into the later fetched opcode at 30.
showcase.check: Run report with fuel 40: Ok after 19 instructions; writes_ahead=True, writes_behind=False, versions=3.
